messages:
alyssa: Heads up — SAST failed on PR #432 (analytics-service). Two findings: one app-level SQL concat, one Terraform IAM/KMS rule in the same PR. Can we triage? :eyes:

sonarcloud-bot: Automated scan results: https://sonar.redwood/scan/7890
- HIGH: SQL_CONCAT_INJECTION in analytics/query_builder.rb:47
- MEDIUM: IAC_AWS_PRIVILEGED_POLICY in infra/iam/analytics.tf:12

alyssa: Paste of the flagged code:
```ruby
# analytics/query_builder.rb:47
query = "SELECT * FROM events WHERE user_id = #{params[:user]}"
# params[:user] is not sanitized here
```

alyssa: And the terraform snippet:
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_policy" "redwood_infra_admin" {
  name = "redwood-infra-admin"
  policy = jsonencode({
    Statement = [{
      Action = "kms:*",
      Resource = "*",
      Effect = "Allow"
    }]
  })
}
```

raj: cc @maria @security-oncall — quick thoughts: app vuln looks like classic SQL injection via string interpolation. If this endpoint accepts user-supplied IDs it must be parameterized. For infra, that policy is too broad (kms:* on *).

maria: Is this PR touching prod deploy pipeline or just staging infra? I see the TF change in `infra/iam/analytics.tf` — that would affect production if merged.

alyssa: It will affect prod when we run the next deploy. The PR touches both `services/analytics` and `infra/iam` — they were grouped because of a refactor.

raj: My recommendation: 1) block merge until app fix or minimal mitigation in place (use paramized query or ActiveRecord binding), 2) revert or tighten IAM policy to least-privilege (limit kms:Encrypt/Decrypt to specific key ARNs, remove wildcard resource), 3) open a vuln ticket and mark P2/P1 depending on exposure, 4) request a DAST run against staging to validate exploitability.

chad: I can run an OWASP ZAP smoke DAST in staging once the branch is deployed. Add a GH action trigger `dast/staging` and I'll kick it off.

maria: Agree with blocking merge. Also ask infra: if we must allow some kms actions for bootstrap, scope to path-less limited key and add `Condition` restricting by `aws:SourceVpce` or `aws:SourceIp`. Also enable KMS key rotation and key usage audit.

raj: On audit logging: we should ensure CloudTrail logging for kms:* events is enabled and shipped to our audit S3 bucket with MFA-delete. Add that to the remediation checklist.

security-oncall: Triage steps I want in the ticket:
- Repro steps and link to PR
- Lines of code & package versions
- Exploitability assessment (DAST result or PoC)
- Suggested remediation and owner (eng/infra)
- Approval gate for merge (security review sign-off)

alyssa: I'll open SECURITY-2974 with the above checklist and assign to @raj and the PR author.

raj: For the SQL issue quick fix example (use parameterized binding):
```ruby
# bad
query = "SELECT * FROM events WHERE user_id = #{params[:user]}"
# good (ActiveRecord)
Event.where(user_id: params[:user])
```

raj: For Terraform policy suggestion:
```hcl
statement {
  actions = ["kms:Encrypt", "kms:Decrypt"]
  resources = ["arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345"]
  condition = { "StringEquals" = { "aws:SourceVpc" = "vpc-0abc123" } }
}
```

maria: Also add an RBAC checklist: if any terraform change touches IAM roles/policies, require 2 approvals (infra + security) and a deploy freeze window if changes touch prod roles.

chad: I'll add the DAST GH action snippet to the PR comments so ops can kick it without extra commits:
```yaml
name: DAST Staging Trigger
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  run-dast:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Trigger staging DAST
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        with:
          script: |
            // call internal tooling to start zap against staging env
```

sonarcloud-bot: Note: suppressing findings requires `sonar.ignore` rule justification. False positives must be documented.

alyssa: I'll mark the ticket with `security:triage` and add the initial notes. Can we set merge rule to block if the `security:triage` label is present?

raj: Yes — repo settings can require `security-review` status check. We should also add a GH action that fails CI when SAST high findings are present unless `security-override` label exists (rare).

maria: One more KMS integration Q — does our CI redact KMS ARNs in logs before sending SAST/DAST outputs to external vendors? We should avoid leaking key ARNs.

raj: Good call. Currently scans redact secrets but not all ARNs. I'll follow up with the SAST vendor to ensure PII/KMS redaction or add a post-scan scrub step in our pipeline.

security-oncall: Assigning SECURITY-2974 -> raj (owner), chad (ops), alyssa (PR author). Target SLA: 72 hours for mitigation plan, 7 days for full remediation.

alyssa: Got it — thanks everyone. I'll open the ticket and paste these snippets + links. :lock:
